title: Julia & Jason's Fringe 2026 Shortlist
subtitle: Edinburgh Festival Fringe · 7–31 August 2026 · curated to taste: drama, music, storytelling, magic and spectacle — strictly no clowns

shows.title: Cathy
shows.why: Elaine C. Smith returns to the Fringe after 26 years — a sharp-tongued widow confronting family secrets. The Traverse is the home of Punch-style new writing.

shows.title: Gameplay
shows.why: Doc-drama about Vasili Arkhipov, the Soviet officer who refused to fire nuclear weapons during the Cuban Missile Crisis.

shows.title: Prophets
shows.why: Psychological thriller: a Scottish researcher meets a religious cult controlling a remote British Overseas Territory. Wicker Man atmosphere.

shows.title: The Second Best School Shooting
shows.acclaim: Produced by Matthew Lillard & Adam McKay
shows.why: Darkly comic play about a real school shooting — hard-hitting in the Punch vein.

shows.title: Badgers
shows.acclaim: Bristol Old Vic / Theatre Royal Plymouth co-production
shows.why: A modern folk tale about a podcaster who digs up something sinister, with live music by Jakabol.

shows.title: Man or Bear
shows.why: Three women navigating persistent male violence, inspired by the viral debate; directed by Ursula Martinez.

shows.title: Mayflies
shows.venue: Rear Warehouse at Brown's of Leith
shows.why: Grid Iron's site-specific adaptation of Andrew O'Hagan's novel, performed in a former Leith metalworks.

shows.title: Mohan: A Partition Story
shows.acclaim: By Fringe First winner Niall Moorjani
shows.why: The writer's grandfather's Partition experience, blended with live music.

shows.title: A Trial – after An Enemy of the People
shows.why: Wagner Moura in a courtroom reimagining of Ibsen — the audience sits as the jury.

shows.title: Book of Shadows
shows.acclaim: From the makers of Fringe hit Space Hippo
shows.why: Occult mystery told entirely through shadow puppetry — for fans of The Ice Hole's lo-fi invention.

shows.title: Dracula: Lucy's Dream
shows.why: Wordless, life-sized-puppetry Dracula told from Lucy's perspective. Extraordinary stagecraft.

shows.title: Elf Lyons is The Woman on the Edge
shows.why: Your past favourite — theatrical show about love, riffing on Vertigo, Apollo 13 and Pagliacci.

shows.title: Kirsty Mann: Corpse
shows.why: Comedian and working doctor tells a real-life ghost story — the Adam Kay slot.

shows.title: Steve Burns: Alive
shows.why: The former Blue's Clues host on parasocial fame and internet mythology.

shows.title: Ahir Shah: Golden
shows.why: Cerebral, moving stand-up — storytelling with real substance.

shows.title: Amanda Knox: Cartwheel
shows.why: Yes, that Amanda Knox — stand-up about her wrongful imprisonment.

shows.title: Susie McCabe: Coming of Rage
shows.why: Glasgow favourite on the health crisis that hit her at 44.

shows.title: Mark Thomas: 40 in Stand-up Years
shows.why: Four decades of political storytelling — as close to spoken word as stand-up gets.

shows.title: Simon Amstell: I Love It Here
shows.why: In town for two nights only.

shows.title: Mr Chonkers: Work in Chonkers
shows.why: John Norris work-in-progress — one late-night one-off.

shows.title: Sh!t Theatre: Evita Too
shows.why: "Hilarious, shambolic" song-driven show about Isabel Perón — smart, musical, very Fringe.

shows.title: Salty Brine: How Strange It Is
shows.why: Acclaimed cabaret storyteller splicing Neutral Milk Hotel's In the Aeroplane Over the Sea with Anne Frank's diary.

shows.title: Tether
shows.why: Scottish-Korean co-production spanning three generations through folk songs, love letters and war stories.

shows.title: Blackbox
shows.why: Hip-hop theatre about Henry "Box" Brown, who mailed himself out of slavery. Great lunchtime slot.

shows.title: Baby Wants Candy
shows.why: A fully improvised musical from an audience-shouted title. Reliably joyous.

shows.title: Kristen Schaal: The Legend of Crystal Shell
shows.why: Comedy play with an original score — Schaal with her Bob's Burgers co-star John Roberts.

shows.title: The Galloping Cure
shows.why: New opera about the opioid crisis — the Punch end of the spectrum, set to music.

shows.title: Bernie Dieter's Club Kabarett
shows.venue: Underbelly's Circus Hub on the Meadows
shows.why: Weimar punk cabaret with sword-swallowing and fire-breathing. Raucous, not clowny — front rows get teased.

shows.title: Ben Hart: The Labyrinth
shows.venue: Palais du Variété, Assembly George Square Gardens
shows.why: Mind-reading and reality-bending with heavy audience involvement — for fans of the pickpocket show.

shows.title: Kevin Quantum: Invisible Force
shows.why: Big-gasp, science-flavoured magic — a strong alternative if Ben Hart's timing doesn't fit.

shows.title: 360 ALLSTARS
shows.why: Urban circus: BMX, basketball, breakdancing, beatboxing, drumming. Scratches the Mythos spectacle itch.

shows.title: Mythos: Ragnarök
shows.why: Norse gods, professional wrestling, hard-rock Viking soundtrack.

shows.title: Loud Poets
shows.why: "Fist-thumping, heart-wrenching" spoken word backed by a live band.

shows.title: Adding Up America: Solving the Race Equation
shows.why: Monique DeBose blending live music, storytelling and sharp social insight.

shows.title: Woodhill
shows.acclaim: Multi-award-winning (Charity Awards; Sheila McKechnie Change Makers Award)
shows.why: LUNG's verbatim dance-theatre about suicides at HMP Woodhill, made with bereaved families — the closest thing at this Fringe to Punch's territory.

shows.title: The Horse of Jenin
shows.acclaim: Fringe First winner · 5★ Guardian · Rolling Stone Top 10
shows.why: Alaa Shehada blends storytelling, mask work and stand-up: a Palestinian boy's resilience, told through a five-metre horse built from debris in Jenin.

shows.title: One Man Musical
shows.acclaim: Guardian's No.1 comedy show of 2024 · Chortle Best Show 2024
shows.why: Flo & Joan's gleeful spoof musical about a certain musical-theatre impresario, starring Edward Easton with the sisters playing live — "better than Cats".

shows.title: Tell Me
shows.why: Sadiq Ali Company (The Chosen Haram): Chinese pole and aerial circus-theatre tracing HIV across two eras. "Stunning, soulful, a total triumph."

shows.title: Ten Thousand Hours
shows.why: Gravity & Other Myths' acrobatic meditation on mastery and the 10,000-hours rule — big-hearted, family-friendly spectacle.

shows.title: James Rowland: Team Viking
shows.acclaim: 5★ Lisa in the Theatre · returning for its 10th anniversary
shows.why: A true story about giving his best mate a Viking funeral — a comic ode to death, friendship and the absurdity of life. Pure Adam Kay territory: storytelling with real substance.

shows.title: My Grandpa Doesn't Follow Me On Instagram
shows.why: Trans storyteller Yoz Mensch retraces a Cornwall-to-Highlands road trip with her grandpa. A trained clown, she uses the craft for character and physicality, not face paint — this is Adam Kay-style storytelling with real substance.

shows.title: John-Luke Roberts: What I Talk About When I Run About, Talking
shows.why: His first new show in four years: surreal wordplay and absurdist stand-up turned on his own health scares and mortality — an endoscopy at 11am on Remembrance Sunday. Weird comedy with real substance underneath.

shows.title: Bog Witch
shows.why: Bryony Kimmings back at the Fringe after seven years, on uprooting her family to a permaculture homestead. “Haunting and hilarious… a climate reckoning of both cosmic and quotidian proportions” — big-tech visual theatre with Lewis Gibson sound design that makes a storm scene startlingly visceral.

shows.title: Sam Nicoresti: Baby Doomer
shows.acclaim: 5★ The Telegraph · 5★ The List · Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Show 2025
shows.why: Angry, absurd and political stand-up built round a misgendering in a department-store changing room — “uproariously funny, life-affirming, dumb and insightful all at once”. Exactly the weird comedy with substance underneath that they go for.

shows.title: Circa: Wolf
shows.venue: The Lafayette, Underbelly's Circus Hub on the Meadows
shows.acclaim: 5★ One4Review · Scotsman critics' best of the 2025 Fringe · reviewed by The Stage
shows.why: Ten Circa acrobats moving as a pack — all instinct and trust — then exploding into gasp-out-loud lifts, jumps and aerials over Ori Lichtik's primal DJ rhythms. The purest hit of the Mythos: Ragnarök spectacle itch at this Fringe.

shows.title: The Pitch
shows.why: East Belfast, a football pitch resurfaced for GAA, and a border poll on the horizon — three teenagers argue out territory, culture and national identity in fast, funny dialogue. The politics is the drama, not decoration on it.

shows.title: Celia Pacquola: Gift Horse
shows.acclaim: 5★ Chortle; Most Outstanding Show, Melbourne Comedy Festival 2026
shows.why: Steve Bennett calls it the Rolls-Royce of stand-up — a gag every couple of lines, craftsmanship hidden under what sounds like conversation. Fast, dense, warm but never soft: the Gilmore Girls signal in stand-up form.

shows.title: Frankie McNair: Huge Ass Mindset
shows.acclaim: 5★ Chortle, 5★ Glam Adelaide; shortlisted for Most Outstanding Show, Melbourne 2026
shows.why: Defiance, not a trauma dump — Chortle calls it proud, powerful and hilarious, vaulting from harrowing to joyously funny. Unsentimental and absurd in the way they like, with none of the cosiness.

shows.title: Andrew White: What a Life!
shows.why: A show about three deaths that refuses to be maudlin — Steve Bennett notes every moment of sentimentality gets knocked back with a gag, for "hard, life-affirming laughs from a place of real heart". Storytelling with substance in the Adam Kay line, and the impishness keeps it well clear of twee.

shows.title: Jenny Gorelick: SORRY
shows.venue: The Studio, Monkey Barrel Comedy (Niddry Street)
shows.why: The vapid-Jersey-girl persona is a disguise for perceptive commentary on gender expectations — why women apologise for everything and men for nothing — and the hour darkens as it goes. Sharp, confident and unsentimental: the Katherine Ryan signal almost exactly.

shows.title: Cecily Hitchcock: Family Recipe
shows.why: A surreal storyteller doing 2000s Britain — New Labour optimism to the crash — and Fest singles out a bit built on 1940s film dialogue: fast, allusive, warm underneath, which is the Gilmore Girls signal. Brazen and high-status rather than charming-and-nothing-else; Katherine Ryan has flagged her too.

shows.title: A Ghost Among the Living
shows.why: Box Tale Soup frame four Poe tales inside a lecture by a scholar whose own dark secret unravels him as he speaks — an academic losing control of his own argument, which is a very Arcadia shape. Handcrafted puppets and masks doing murder and madness, commissioned off real archive research at UCLA's Clark Library. Gothic and unsettling, nowhere near twee.

shows.title: Kate Dehnert: Echo
shows.why: A breakup show with the sentiment burned off — Dehnert bills it as a third play, a third stand-up, a third rave, and Chortle calls it "relentlessly fast", swinging from fury to silly in a beat. Rage about being left, played as force rather than fragility: the Katherine Ryan register, and about as far from twee as the Fringe gets.

shows.title: Lara Ricote: INKLING
shows.why: An hour built out from the three Delphic maxims into a genuine argument about what it is to exist — a withering routine on atheists, a Buddhist parable acted out, people sorted into free-spirited "naked babies" and clothed ones. Chortle calls it thought-provoking and hilarious in the same breath, which is the Arcadia shape in stand-up form. Ricote describes herself as a clown, but this is philosophising at speed, not a clown persona piece — flagged rather than dropped.

shows.title: Bunny!
shows.why: Craig Manson's murderous aspiring starlet, told through Broadway parodies and a tonal pivot from bright opener to outright horror — a satire on the brutality of making it in the arts, from the man whose Instagram eviscerates arts-organisation nonsense. High camp, but sardonic rather than cosy: unsentimental bite in the Katherine Ryan register, with none of the twee. Cabaret character piece, not a clown persona show.

shows.title: Paul Foot: The Future
shows.why: Alt-comedy's great eccentric builds an hour out of niche statistics into an actual argument — that our appetite for cruelty, not scarcity, is what keeps the socio-economic future bleak — with his Jewish grandmother's suitcase from her escape from Nazi Germany at its centre. Absurdism doing the work of a thesis rather than decorating one, which is the Arcadia signal in stand-up form; Fest calls it "unexpectedly rousing". Weird and acerbic, nowhere near twee.

shows.title: Overtone
shows.acclaim: 4★ The Stage; WhatsOnStage: "a devastating, deeply reflective piece of theatre"
shows.why: Hard-hitting new drama in the Punch mould — a non-linear two-hander on the aftermath of a coercive choirmaster, from Fringe First winner Tom Brennan. "Terrifically tightly wound performances" wrestling with "prickly, profound questions"; opens comic and direct-address, builds to a shocking close. No sentimentality anywhere near it.

shows.title: For Dolores
shows.acclaim: 5★ The Arts Review · 5★ BroadwayWorld · 4★ The Guardian · Irish Times rave
shows.why: Eva O'Connor two-hander for Fishamble (four-time Fringe First winners) — two friends, one Scottish, one Irish, reckoning with addiction, motherhood and the worst thing they ever did. "Funny, bruising and brilliantly written and acted" (Irish Times): the wit and the damage in the same line, which is the Traverse doing what Punch did.

shows.title: Non Human Animal
shows.acclaim: 4★ The Stage (Lyn Gardner, 9 Aug): "fierce and spiked with dark humour"
shows.why: Kat Woods' semi-autobiographical Northern Irish drama: a playwright whose father was murdered is asked to meet his killer, while her mother's dementia closes in. An argument play — victim trauma against offender rehabilitation, and what happens when forgiveness does not heal — carried on dark wit rather than uplift, with a heroine who compares herself to Batman and binges Gilmore Girls. Gardner: "Woods speaks up; perhaps it's time we listened?"

shows.title: Bliss
shows.why: A fairy tale taken apart rather than served up warm: four over-educated sisters let out of their tower, a razor-sharp book about the price of perfection, and a pop-rock score with actual bite. The biggest new musical of the Fringe, and subversive where it could have been sweet.

shows.title: Water Colour
shows.acclaim: 4★ The Scotsman (Joyce McMillan) · 5★ The Stage (Pitlochry staging) · CATS Best New Play 2026
shows.why: Milly Sweeney's multi-award-winning debut: Esme, stalled on her Glasgow School of Art MA, meets Harris, a chef with a tidy job and a life shifting under him, once on a bridge over the Clyde — then the play follows them separately for months as they never meet again. Poetic and bracingly vernacular in the same breath, mulling life and death without a shred of uplift; the Traverse doing what Punch did. McMillan: "a vital dispatch from the front line of the mental health crisis among young people... and a memorable strand of pure poetry".

shows.title: Harriet Dyer: Easily Distra…
shows.why: An hour so densely packed the reviewer reckons an average comedian could stretch it into three shows — chaotic, tangential, fast, with a sixth sense for the right sound and face. The dense-allusive-dialogue signal, in stand-up form.

shows.title: Harriet Richardson: Creep
shows.why: Debut hour on parasocial obsession that Fest calls bold, anarchic and deeply incisive — stand-up braided with performance art, shame and attraction dissected rather than cuddled. Sharp and unsentimental, the Katherine Ryan register.

shows.title: Andrew Doherty: Reviewers Welcome... TO DIE!
shows.acclaim: 4★ Time Out, 4★ The Guardian, 4★ The Scotsman
shows.why: A slasher-movie pastiche in which a critic who gave Doherty three stars is hunted through a Lovecraftian town — Time Out calls it an ebullient, horror-tinged celebration of being a hater, the Guardian the finest horror pastiche on the Fringe since Garth Marenghi. Fast, allusive, gleefully petty: bite rather than warmth, and not a trace of twee.

shows.title: Supposing:
shows.acclaim: 4★ The Stage (Lyn Gardner) · 4★ All Edinburgh Theatre · WhatsOnStage: "subtle, slow-burning power"
shows.why: Zinnie Harris writes and directs a modern Cassandra: Sally falls down a hole, comes up able to see what is coming, and nobody believes her. Greek myth used as an argument about belief, evidence and a society's willed blindness to injustice — the ideas are the drama, not decoration on it, and Harris plays it dark and comic rather than earnest. Gardner: "quietly effective and deftly done".

shows.title: Kate Dolan: Trout
shows.acclaim: 4★ Fest · 4★ Chortle · 4★ The Scotsman · Melbourne Comedy Festival Director's Choice winner 2026
shows.why: Absurdist stand-up at full tilt — a gazillion accents, dance breaks, a silicone fish helmet — but Fest notes the gear change at 45 minutes that puts a real emotional throughline under the chaos: “a madcap hour which impressively balances chaotic vibes with a strong emotional throughline”. Chortle says her performance “screams star quality”, the Scotsman “irrepressibly funny”. Weird-and-absurd comedy done with craft, chaotic rather than cosy. It borrows physical technique, but this is stand-up, not a clown persona piece.

shows.title: Rob Preston: Amazing Global Solutions
shows.why: Debut character hour: a gallery of modern grotesques — influencer-bros, corporate stooges — taken past cliché to farcical limits. Fest praises the “comedic peacocking” and the men “cucked by their own emotional insecurities”: satire of masculinity with the knife out and no warmth offered as consolation. Sharp and unsentimental, the Katherine Ryan register.

shows.title: The Plot
shows.why: Emma Howlett's world premiere reopens the Gunpowder Plot as a fight over who gets to write the story — courtroom drama, backstage comedy and Shakespeare folded into one 70-minute argument about spin, myth-making and who controls history. The Stage calls it a "slippery, shifting study" and "thrillingly smart riff on conspiracy, spin and Shakespeare", signing off "Remember, remember the name Emma Howlett. She is going places." The ideas are the drama, not decoration on it — the Arcadia signal, done with wit rather than earnestness.

shows.title: The Jolly Fisherman
shows.why: John Dinneen's world premiere two-hander: boyhood friends Alan and Amir in East London, and the pub of the title turning into a mosque. The argument about who a shared space belongs to is the play, not a backdrop to it — belonging, faith and a changing city fought out between two people who love each other. The Stage calls it an "engrossing two-hander", "deft, propulsive, detailed and funny": the hard-hitting new drama register of Punch, with the wit kept in.

shows.title: This Is Not America
shows.why: Philip Stokes's world-premiere thriller: a body in a Brooklyn house, three identical brothers hauled in for questioning, and Jack Stokes playing every one of them — switching voice and body between interrogations until truth, identity and power come apart. Theatre Weekly calls it "one of the strongest dramas at this year’s Fringe" and Stokes's work "one of the most electrifying performances in Edinburgh this year", with a final act of "terrifying force". Hard-hitting new drama in the Punch register, and the argument about American myth-making is the play rather than its setting.

shows.title: Ethan & Gigi Present: THE MOVEMENT
shows.why: Two overconfident American theatremakers set out to liberate the masses through the power of theatre and undermine themselves at every turn — a mock-heroic demolition of revolutionary art, political posturing and the form itself. Fest calls the Hamilton parody "the single funniest thing I’ve ever seen" and credits "superior comedic writing" behind the chaos, signing off "Vive THE MOVEMENT". Weird, absurd and satirical with real bite, nothing gentle about it. Flagged: the company tags itself Clown/Alternative Comedy, but the show is a written two-hander satire rather than a red-nose persona piece, so it stays in per the no-clowns rule.

shows.title: Buggers
shows.why: Alistair Hall's psychodrama on Francis Bacon and George Dyer, built as a triptych to echo Bacon's own form — hard-hitting new drama in the Punch register, unsentimental and formally clever rather than warm.

shows.title: Jack Brookmyre: Impressionable
shows.why: An impressionist hour that is really an argument about accents — how a voice decides whether we trust a politician — with the impressions carrying the thesis rather than decorating it. Fest, openly sceptical going in, came out praising “whip-smart storytelling, savvy observations and caustic gags”. Caustic and idea-led rather than warm: the Katherine Ryan register with something to say.

shows.title: Demi Adejuyigbe Sells Out
shows.why: Songs, sketches, one-liners and audience interaction welded onto a bit about selling out for money — controlled chaos held together by, in Fest’s words, “super sharp comebacks” and a performer confident enough to run genuinely risky material. Weird, fast and deliciously silly, with the wit doing the work rather than charm.

shows.title: PLASTIC
shows.why: Minyoung Kim plays the geomungo — the ancient Korean zither — against electronics and jeongga poetry-song, with psychedelic projection, building an argument about climate collapse and cultural inheritance out of the collision of the two. Fest calls it “a startlingly cinematic journey” and comes out the other side calling it cathartic. Gig-theatre with real intellectual weight; austere and strange rather than pretty.

shows.title: Frankie Thompson: Horrible Things
shows.why: Thompson lipsyncs her way through a grotesque, meticulously built persona — Time Out likens her to Queenie from Blackadder, "a posh, slightly eccentric despot" — and turns it on people in power. Absurd, formally restless, politically sharp, and nowhere near cosy: the register is Katherine Ryan's unsentimental bite arriving by a much stranger route. Time Out's five stars call it "phenomenal". Note on the no-clowns rule: the copy calls her an "avant-clown", but this is character and performance-art comedy that draws on clown technique, not a red-nose persona piece — kept deliberately.

shows.title: Amy Matthews: Definitions of Toast
shows.why: Chortle calls it the hour where everything clicks into place — "smart, clinical wit, emotional vulnerability" from a comic writing about rage she cannot access. The clinical wit is the Katherine Ryan register, sharp rather than consoling.

shows.title: ALONE
shows.why: Two women — a pilot and a scientist — trapped on a failing spacecraft, with The Stage praising a script that "skilfully and shrewdly explores themes ranging from misogyny in science to the climate emergency". Ideas-driven two-hander where the argument is the drama, and it ends in darkness rather than reassurance.

shows.title: DUSK/NIGHT/DAWN
shows.why: NYC collective Vertical Dreamscape turn pole into serious stagecraft — a dark, cinematic night-shift dreamscape that Theatre Weekly calls physical theatre, dance and visual art at once. Spectacle with an edge, nowhere near twee; the same slot as Circa: Wolf.

shows.title: Will Adamsdale: AI, AI, Oh…
shows.acclaim: The Scotsman — "narrative comedy at its peak"
shows.why: The Perrier winner's true(ish) robo-bromance about writing a sitcom with ChatGPT — The Scotsman says watching him is "like watching Fred Astaire, at his peak, tapdance", with "tiny verbal callbacks seeded through" beautifully crafted prose. Absurd premise carrying a real argument about technology: ideas and wit in the same breath.

shows.title: Scout Boxall: God's Favourite
shows.acclaim: 5★ Time Out, 4★ Chortle, 4★ The List; The Scotsman — "cuttingly funny above all else"
shows.why: A dark night of the soul told through Joan of Arc and Hildegard of Bingen — Chortle calls it "an evocative piece of magical realism storytelling" rather than stand-up, and The Scotsman finds it "cuttingly funny above all else". Dense, allusive and unsentimental: the Katherine Ryan edge with the reading behind it.

shows.title: Bebe Cave: Swoon
shows.why: Character comedy that takes apart the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood — "skewers pretentious male artistry and the women they love to drown", asking why the women are only beautiful once dead while the men stay difficult and alive. Chortle calls it "cuttingly relevant and joyously daft". An argument about art history delivered as jokes: Arcadia-adjacent ideas with a Katherine Ryan edge.

shows.title: Sophie Duker: Hot Beef Injection
shows.acclaim: 4★ The Scotsman, The Telegraph, The Times, Fest, The Skinny & Evening Standard
shows.why: Stand-up on sex and privilege — "brilliantly crafted takes on toxic men", with "airtight writing and effortless confidence", and "so neatly crafted and intelligent that every routine serves a purpose". Seven four-star notices from major outlets and not a gentle one among them: this is squarely the sharp, confident, unsentimental Katherine Ryan register.

shows.title: Alice Fraser: Oh Man!
shows.venue: Monkey Barrel Comedy at O'Neill's (The Tron)
shows.acclaim: 5★ Broadway Baby & EdinburghGuide; 4.5★ Edinburgh Reviews; rave in BroadwayWorld
shows.why: Fraser takes on the manosphere with a sentient Roomba and Ancient Greek philosophy — "an intellectually rich hour" blending philosophy, social commentary and sharp observational comedy, "cutting-edge" rather than consoling. Ideas that ARE the comedy, done with real craft: the Arcadia signal in stand-up form, and Jason the philosopher gets the Greeks thrown in.

shows.title: Amanda Dwyer: Better Than Revenge
shows.why: A debut about grudges and payback that refuses the easy catharsis of the survivor narrative — Fest calls it "caustic, complicated", and notes she "isn't some people-pleasing comedian trying to win over an audience", taking you instead "through shame, rage and what comes after". Sharp and unsentimental where the material invites sentiment: the Katherine Ryan register exactly.

shows.title: Krapp's Last Tape
shows.why: Beckett's man dissected across time — a 69-year-old listening back to the tapes of his younger, hopeful self, and growling at him. Ideas as the drama, not decoration; bleak and exact, with no whimsy anywhere near it. David Westhead's performance is Fest's 'exceptional', and it is Stockard Channing's directorial debut at 82.

shows.title: Olga Koch: Fat Tom Cruise
shows.why: Koch tells one story that is not hers, cutting between the present and the 1970s — fraternity hazing, the ACLU, the Hague — to get at fear and gender. Sharp, unsentimental, and genuinely about something: the ideas are the show, not decoration on it. Three notices in three days and not a whiff of the cosy register.

shows.title: Lou Wall: Where Are All The Tall Grandmas?
shows.why: A properly researched absurd question — where did the tall old women go? — chased through multimedia, data and family history until it turns into something about difference and inheritance. Dense, fast and driven by curiosity rather than charm; the review calls it 'geeky' and says it leaves you feeling 'intelligent, surprised, positive and giggly'. Investigation as comedy, with no cosiness in it.

doNotReadd.title: Bigfoot Ripped My Dog In Half I Saw It
Mythos: Ragnarök
doNotReadd.reason: already seen in a previous year

doNotReadd.title: Garry Starr: Classic Penguins
doNotReadd.reason: 5★ The Stage, but the show is the Garry Starr clown persona itself — top hat, tails and flippers, physical stunts on classic novels. Clowning is what the show is, not a technique it borrows.

doNotReadd.title: Sammy J: Hero Complex
doNotReadd.reason: Marketed as five-star, but the actual Fringe 2026 notice is Chortle 3.5★ (Tim Harding, 8 Aug): "exuberant innocence and gentle laughs", an earnest dorky persona, "a dispatch from a blessedly less edgy era". Structurally masterful storytelling, but the tone is precisely the gentle/twee register ruled out.

doNotReadd.title: House Fly
doNotReadd.reason: 4★ Fest, but it is a fly-drag clown persona piece from clown Tess O'Shea — "unstoppably silly, gleeful". Clowning is what the show is, and the register is the gleeful/twee one ruled out.

doNotReadd.title: Dee Allum: Raumdeuter
doNotReadd.reason: 4★ Fest (also reviewed by Chortle), but the verdict is "admirably honest, upbeat stand-up is a joy to spend time with" — warm and gentle rather than sharp. Cosiness without edge.

doNotReadd.title: House of Life
doNotReadd.reason: 4★ Fest (8 Aug), but the verdict is an "irresistibly earnest rally cry for joy" — a rave-church cabaret whose satire of self-help serves a sincere uplift. Joyful-celebration register, ruled out.

doNotReadd.title: Jonathan Oldfield: Exquisite Corpse
doNotReadd.reason: 4★ Fest (10 Aug), sketch and character comedy praised as "utterly singular in its unpredictable joy" with "unique warmth" — gentle and whimsical in register. Cosiness without edge, ruled out.

doNotReadd.title: Dane Buckley: Darling
doNotReadd.reason: 5★ The Skinny (10 Aug), debut hour about the women who raised him — but reviewed as "a warm hug of a show: an explosive celebration of queerness, family and heritage", heartfelt rather than biting. Warmth in place of edge, ruled out.

doNotReadd.title: Shotgunned
doNotReadd.reason: The “5★ The Stage” on the edfringe page is a marketing quote from the sold-out 2024 run, not a Fringe 2026 notice. The actual 2026 review is Theatre Weekly 4★ (8 Aug) and lukewarm — a non-linear relationship two-hander on “familiar territory”, the reviewer asking “what is the actual point of this play?” before the ending redeems it. Heartfelt and endearing rather than sharp; warmth without bite.

doNotReadd.title: Freddie Meredith: Need A Light?
doNotReadd.reason: Chortle 4★ (Steve Bennett, 9 Aug) for an assured debut, but the show is a lonely, insecure alter-ego styling out his insecurities in a nightclub smoking area — the humour is "exquisitely realistic" observation rather than satire, and the review turns on sympathy for his "intrinsic sadness" and a "slightly hopeful resolution". Poignant sad-sack character comedy: warmth in place of bite.
